successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: 'most of the Swiss plateau at the time of their contact with the Roman Republic in the 1st century BC': the cantons between Lake Geneva, the Jura, the Rhine and the Alps' foothills

ledger.x: Late 2nd century BC: the Helvetii settle the Swiss plateau.
58 BC: the Helvetii march west and meet Caesar.
58 BC: the Helvetii fall under Rome as an allied people.
58 BC: the independent Helvetii end at Bibracte; the civitas lives on as a Roman ally and later a colony.

wars.name: Battle of Bibracte
wars.outcome: Roman victory: the Helvetii and their allies surrendered; Caesar claimed 130,000 got away, 110,000 of whom returned home; the Helvetii became foederati.

certainty.note: The page gives no borders; the plateau between Lake Geneva, the Jura and the Rhine is the researcher's reading.
